items.title: Hello, I’m Ruoshui!
items.text: I’m a second-year Computer Science Specialist at the University of Toronto. The problems that hook me are the ones that work on paper and fall apart in practice: a slow algorithm, a bug that only shows up when several systems meet, or an AI model that gets the right answer for the wrong reason.

items.title: Education
items.text: I’m at the University of Toronto, working toward a B.Sc. in Computer Science (Specialist) with a Classics major in Greek and Latin. I’m expected to graduate in June 2029, with a cGPA of 4.0/4.0.

items.title: What I’m Exploring
items.text: Lately I keep coming back to one question: why do AI systems fail, and how do we make them faster, easier to test, and more trustworthy? I’m also curious about formal methods and verification, especially where they meet AI and real software.

items.title: Language & Structure
items.text: I study Ancient Greek and Latin alongside CS, and to me they feel like the same hobby: rules, exceptions, and working out how a complicated system fits together. It has also made me wonder whether language models actually learn grammatical structure, or mostly repeat patterns they have seen before.

items.title: Making Things
items.text: Outside of class, I’m usually making something: VR games, interactive web projects, illustration, animation, video editing, even fan merchandise. I sold my own work at conventions from 2023 to 2025, and I still take illustration commissions online.

items.title: Research
items.text: I’m still figuring out exactly where I want to specialize, but I know I like problems where reasoning meets building and debugging real systems. I’d love to get research experience as an undergraduate, and eventually go on to a research-focused graduate degree in computer science.

items.title: Award
items.text: International Merit Admission Award from the Faculty of Arts & Science, received in 2025–26 and renewed for 2026–27.

items.title: Languages
items.text: Mandarin is my first language, English is my fluent second, and I’m studying Ancient Greek and Latin.

items.title: Current Interests
items.text: ML systems · Reliable AI · AI evaluation · Formal methods · Algorithms · Language-model reasoning.

items.title: AACorn · Visual AAC Communication Board
items.text: I’m leading a student team building AACorn, an accessible visual communication board in Java. I own the message-building logic and help keep architecture, integration, and development moving together.

items.title: Bird Species Interaction Network
items.text: A four-person project that turned 6,000 iNaturalist observations into a graph of seasonal bird co-occurrence. I built the core weighted-graph algorithm in Python, then went back and reworked the graph construction to cut redundant species-pair comparisons, which made interactive analysis practical.

items.title: Team Cobalt · VR Game
items.text: I joined an OCAD student VR team in the last week of development and led implementation, integration, and debugging of the core Unity/C# gameplay systems. The finished game was exhibited at VRTO 2026.

items.title: Ocean Portfolio
items.text: You’re looking at it. The concept and artwork are my own, built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, CSS, and SVG. I used AI-assisted coding throughout, but I read, debug, and test what it produces before anything goes in.

items.title: Zhiyuan Robotics · Intern
items.text: As a robotics testing and validation intern in Shanghai, I prepared test sets, reviewed system outputs, and documented the discrepancies I found so engineers could follow up.

items.title: Pattern Recognition Project
items.text: Before university, I tried PCA- and SVM-based face recognition in Python with OpenCV, scikit-learn, and NumPy, mostly working on preprocessing and feature extraction.

items.title: Film Archive & Translation
items.text: I translate and technically edit bilingual subtitles for historical and international films, handling timing, encoding, and quality control. Some of the releases have reached more than 10,000 downloads.
